I ran into this same issue yesterday while trying to run a custom agent. After digging around, it looks like this is a known side effect of OpenCode's V1 → V2 migration — agent configs defined the old way won't work under V2 without updating the permission format.

For reference, here's a simple code reviewer agent definition:

**V1 (old) permission format:**

```md
---
description: Primary review agent that validates implementation quality and creates comprehensive test scenarios
mode: primary
model: opencode/mimo-v2.5-free
temperature: 0.1
permission:
  read: allow
  edit: deny
  bash: deny
---

You are the Primary Review Agent responsible for validating implementation quality and creating comprehensive test scenarios.
```

**V2 (new) permission format:**

```md
---
description: Primary review agent that validates implementation quality and creates comprehensive test scenarios
mode: primary
model: opencode/mimo-v2.5-free
permissions:
  - action: read
    resource: "*"
    effect: allow
  - action: edit
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: bash
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
---

You are the Primary Review Agent responsible for validating implementation quality and creating comprehensive test scenarios.
```

Switching to the V2 permission block (array of `{action, resource, effect}` objects instead of the flat `permission` map) fixed it for me. This isn't a bug on OpenCode's end — it's purely a migration issue on the agent config side.

Docs: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/#permissions-and-tools

## Decisive evidence: the subscription is on this account, and the Console still can't see it

Adding three findings that should narrow this down.

### 1. The payment receipt confirms this account is the subscriber

The Console login account (`742840609@qq.com`) received an OpenCode receipt:

- Amount: **US$10.00** (the Go monthly price)
- Paid: **2026-09-08 13:27 (GMT+8)** = **2026-09-08 05:27 UTC**
- Method: Alipay
- Receipt no. `2374-8861`, invoice no. `TYOCW30L-0001`

### 2. The billing anchor matches the Go usage API exactly

The Go usage API's monthly window resets exactly one month after that payment, to the second:

```
GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage
"monthly": { "status": "ok", "percent": 41, "resetsAt": "2026-10-08T05:27:23.880Z" }
```

Payment `2026-09-08 05:27 UTC` → monthly reset `2026-10-08T05:27:23Z`. Same day-of-month, same time-of-day, one month apart.

So the $10 Alipay payment on 2026-09-08 **is** the Go subscription, and it is attached to this account.

### 3. `opencode console login` succeeds but does not fix the Console

I re-ran the CLI login; device authorization completed:

```
$ opencode console login
  Go to: https://opencode.ai/console/device?user_code=WKXV-RBCC&client_id=opencode-cli
  Enter code: WKXV-RBCC
  Logged in as 742840609@qq.com
```

The device page showed access to **"All workspaces"**. After this, the Console is unchanged:

- `Personal` (`org_01M2X03EH8BXK2MFVV7CDZQGG4`) → Go tab still shows **Subscribe**
- `111` (`org_01M2X2BK4M7P02N2BHARZRTGZR`) → Go tab also shows **Subscribe**
- Both orgs' Overview: `$0.00` / 0 requests / 0 tokens
- Neither org's workspace switcher lists any workspace

### 4. This account has two orgs, and both are blind to the subscription

```
$ opencode console orgs
● Personal  742840609@qq.com  org_01M2X03EH8BXK2MFVV7CDZQGG4   (active)
  111       742840609@qq.com  org_01M2X2BK4M7P02N2BHARZRTGZR
```

The old workspace `wrk_01KVMTCRN3NBTCBN2ZDK21MV29` is unreachable: `/workspace/<wrk>/go` → 302 to auth, `/console/<wrk>/go` → blank page.

Meanwhile the Go usage API still returns live data for this account (rolling 5% / weekly 46% / monthly 41% used), and a third-party plugin reading the same `auth.json` key reports 95% / 54% / 59% left.

### Conclusion

The subscription exists and is billing this account — the receipt and the API's reset anchor prove it — but the Console cannot resolve the workspace it belongs to, in either org. This looks like a `wrk_` → `org_` workspace migration/loading failure specific to this account.

### Side note (separate issue, but related infra)

Every recent `triage` workflow run in this repo is failing with `Error: Upstream request failed: Insufficient account funds`, so new issues are not being auto-labeled. Might be worth a look on its own.

To be more specific, OpenCode is not parsing/executing DSML tool calls made by Deepseek V4.1 Flash **when it is used with Opencode Go**. The same model served by OpenRouter does **not** have the same problem, because OpenRouter intercept DSML tool calls and convert them to a more standard JSON format automatically.

- If it is a tool call from which the DeepSeek model expects a response the turn will often end, without explanation.

- If it is a tool call that the model expects to make changes, like editing a file, it can causes bugs and confusion because it assumes the change was made successfully (since there were no errors), when nothing has actually happened.

This was previously reported (#24566) but Closed As Not Planned. I hope this was a misunderstanding, as it seems irresponsible to include DeepSeek models in the Opencode Go subscription when its tool call format is not supported.

Thanks for walking through the two reconciliation runs — the independent methods landing at 42% and 84% was the useful signal, since they fail independently. On the structural fix, I'd use two-level attribution on the session record — own_cost (tokens the root agent billed directly) and total_cost (own plus descendants, resolved by one parent_id walk). The sidebar shows total_cost, per-message views own_cost, and total - own = sum(children own_cost) becomes a checkable invariant, not a spreadsheet. A recursive walk over existing history keeps it cheap and makes the gap self-evident in `opencode stats`. On your ask: DELEGATION-001 captures the rollup omission but not the hidden-call bypass (summaries/titles never reach the message flow); the reconciliation shape was an append-only event log cross-checked against cached rollups — happy to share both query shapes.

> Removing `"bash": "deny"` from my agent config fixed it for me.

Just to clarify — removing `"bash": "deny"` isn’t really fixing the sub-agent issue. What it’s actually doing is **granting the main agent the `bash` permission it was missing**, which changes the request signature enough to pass the free-tier classifier.

The underlying problem is still there: the free-tier entitlement gate rejects sub-agent requests based on their tool/permission set, regardless of whether the sub-agent actually needs `bash`. The `explore` agent is intentionally read-only and should never have shell access, yet it fails with the same 403 — while `general` with identical models succeeds.

So the workaround "works" by sidestepping the classifier, but it doesn’t address the root cause: **sub-agent requests should be classified the same as primary agent requests when using the same free-tier models from within the CLI.**

`client.close()` terminates the direct transport child, but the outer `cmd.exe /d /s /c "npx ..."` and the package's own `cmd.exe` both stay alive, so the wrapper tree outlives the disconnect exactly as you describe. That's a strange direction for a product built on an open-source, transparency-first project. Users should be able to see exactly how their usage is being measured, especially when there's an open, unresolved question about whether that measurement is even correct.
